newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr expected to rise in Asia but still top-heavy.
newsitem.headline: Dlr expected to rise in Asia but still top-heavy.

text.p: The dollar is expected to edge higher during Asian trading time on Tuesday, but the topside will remain heavy, keeping gains capped at around 124.50 yen.
Although the dollar had risen to around 123.90 yen in early Asian trade after stop-loss buying was triggered near 123.80 yen, exporter sales near 124 yen flat are expected to limit gains temporarily.

"If the dollar continues to rise, these offers are likely to be withdrawn to a higher level, perhaps around 124.50 yen," a credit bank dealer said. But a trust bank dealer said there did not appear to be significant offers near 124 yen.
"There's nothing especially significant about 124 yen. The fact that the dollar rose above 123.80 yen, where there were offers on Monday, is more important and could signal further gains," he added.
The credit bank dealer said that should the dollar hit 124 yen before 9 a.m. (0000 GMT), it was likely to remain strong above that level.
Additional topside heaviness is expected from sterling's overnight losses against the yen and the mark on news that British Prime Minister John Major was calling a general election on May 1.
Bids are expected from securities firms and trust banks, dealers said.

Uncertainties about the starting date of European economic and monetary union (EMU) after German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday that strict adherence to criteria for the single currency was more important than the 1999 timetable helped lift the mark above 73 yen and buoyed it against other European currencies.
But rises any higher than around 73.20 yen are expected to be hard, limiting dollar moves against the yen. "Cross trading is likely to keep on leading trade today," a dealer said.
Against the mark, buying of the dollar on dips emerged to help lift the greenback slightly overnight, along with short-covering.
But the fact that the dollar fell as low as 1.6840 marks in New York trade suggests it remains unstable, with gains in Tokyo trade expected to be limited.
A Japanese market holiday on March 20 is also likely to depress trading interest, dealers said.
